findings.text: The split is behaviour-preserving for the full path. retain_logical_class_body_sources now runs the factory pass and then a body pass. A class that does not match still clears all four facets: the factory pass clears coordinate, name and relations, and the body closure's '?' yields None for body. The match is computed twice, which is cheap.

self.registry is profile_registry() = analysis_context().commands(), the same store that produce_object_handle_facts receives in the full path, so registry provenance is consistent. The disjoint field borrow (self.registry vs self.result) compiles.

The fix targets the cause correctly. OriginalProjectProcedureRoles::capture requires source_candidate_coordinate() for every class header, and the structure-only path never set it. This is consistent with DB 35r2 test-001 (project_proc_var_index_for_inputs empty) and with the existing HEAD control logical_members.rs:1653.

The new section says the facets 'do not depend on emitting diagnostics or building a compilation unit'. In full (non-structural) analysis they are still produced only inside produce_object_handle_facts, which runs after the CU build under catch_unwind and the early-return gates of emit_cfg_ssa_diagnostics. Either reword the section or document that the full path keeps its CU dependency. The paragraph is also one unwrapped line, unlike the surrounding ~80-column text.

The control is weak. It never shows that the full path still issues a body, for example by asserting full_owner.original_body_word(...).is_some(). The 'different' image assertion is vacuous because image inequality alone returns None.

findings.text: Without V2, V1 promotes Complete and extends occurrences over existing reference_spans positives that the census never accounted for. These are external receiver queries, which is a missing-to-complete promotion. The author and the peer both state this.

The Partial property branch was hand-compacted ('identity.uri(), source, analysis,' on one line, ').as_ref() == Some(identity)).then_some(...)'). rustfmt leaves it in place because it gives up on the enclosing expression, so it passes fmt but is not idiomatic. Restore the standard layout.
Silent narrowing: property identities with object_owner.is_some() lose the census path, which the old property branch allowed, and now always report Partial. This is conservative but undocumented.
The contract text contains process narrative ('actual replay is required', 'this bounded prerequisite', 'fixture remains explicitly unresolved'). AGENTS.md requires that to be removed before a PR.

The '{source}; mystery' assertion is vacuous for the census. It returns None only through identity currency, because the source differs. The third block, 'my target; mystery', does exercise the unknown-head barrier.

In tcl8.6 this original test asserts coverage == Partial for 'oo::class create C {method ping {} {}; method body {} {my ping; my ping}}'. It also asserts reference_spans is empty, so V2's all(contains) gate is satisfied vacuously. V1's own new control (line 2282) asserts CompleteSourceOccurrenceCensus for the structurally identical 'oo::class create C {method target {} {}; method owner {} {my target}}' in tcl8.6. Both cannot hold. If the census works as designed, original line 1721 flips to red, which is an assertion regression by behaviour. If it does not, the new control is red.

The code-lens originals require exact counts ('2 references', '0 references') for the same tcl8.6 shape. That needs Complete, which is the opposite of test-096's Partial. This is a locked same-input contradiction between original assertions, like Compiler221. It needs an explicit user decision. The census must not resolve it silently by flipping test-096.

V2's new control is probably non-discriminating. 'C create c' and 'c target' have heads with no selected Registry source schema, so source_registry_words(...)? already aborts the census before either V2 veto or the all(contains) gate runs. The control would pass on HEAD, on V1 alone and on V2. Add a fixture in which a registry-selected head carries an object receiver or query and the self census alone would otherwise be complete.

The vetoes return None for the whole census from inside the non-self branch. This is fail-closed and fine. Static typing checks out: class_at_command_head and method_at_command take &SegmentedCommand; OriginalMethodQuery::span() returns Span, compared with argv[1].span.

No compile risk found. SourceSyntaxCoverage::{capture, applicability, commands} exist and are exported at lib.rs:109. definition_member_at returns Result<Option<_>>. OriginalDeclarationIdentity implements PartialEq. command_span() is Option for method rows and Span for property rows, and the code handles both. No dead code results, because visit_checked_analysis_executable_commands is still used in receiver_identity.rs:655.

The adapter is genuine. tcl_spectcl::core_surfaces::ensure() is the same public initializer the server's initialize handler calls (tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs:30086). It is inserted before the unchanged CommandRegistry::build_default() and fixture, and every value and assertion is byte-identical. The compiled-in Jim roster omits coroutine, so the original assertion at :7875 can now hold for the real reason.

This creates a dev-dependency cycle, because tcl-spectcl depends on tcl-lsp-core (tcl-spectcl/Cargo.toml:41). Cargo permits it, and tcl-registry and tcl-compiler already do the same, each with a 'A dev-dependency cycle ... which Cargo permits' rationale comment. This entry has no comment; add one. project-layout.md:83 says the tcl-spectcl edge 'introduces no cycle', so consider a sentence there too. No #[no_mangle] or links key exists in tcl-lsp-core, so the duplicate crate copy in the test binary causes no symbol clash. The Cargo.lock entry is correctly placed and sorted.

The selector-per-process capture harness cannot detect this. I found no specific dependent assertion: sampled Jim loops use only rostered commands.
